 Technology Alibaba trains next-gen AI model on own chips amid tighter US curbs
 Chinese tech company's quarterly profit more than triples as cloud services boost sales
 Alibaba's stock price has fallen more than 40% since the start of the year. © Reuters
 CISSY ZHOU November 19, 2026 20:27 JST Updated on November 19, 2026 23:13 JST HONG KONG -- Facing tightened access to advanced U.S. artificial intelligence chips, Alibaba Group is already training its next-generation AI model on proprietary chips from T-Head, the company's chip unit that recently was approved for an IPO in Hong Kong, CEO Eddie Wu said on Thursday.
